subject: Partner adapter compatibility policy and deprecation timeline — Orbis Ecosystems
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbis-ecosys.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: partners@orbis-ecosys.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood API changes — impact to Orbis adapter

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the recent roadmap brief. We reviewed the outline around the tokenization and /v1/streams changes and have a couple of asks from the Orbis side before we schedule engineering alignment:

- Can you share the formal deprecation policy you intend to apply to public inference endpoints (minimum notice window, intended semver boundaries, and end-of-life process)?
- We maintain a partner adapter (Orbis Redwood Adapter, v1.6.2) that plugs into customer infra; we need a compatibility matrix we can compare against our automated test suite.
- Any plan for automatic fallback behavior or staged rollouts that would affect customers using the adapter (especially for Dedicated tenants)?

I've attached our current adapter matrix (orbis-adapter-matrix.xlsx) showing which API surface we call and our in-flight work to support streaming multiplexed responses. A short sync next week would be great — prefer Wed or Thu morning PT.

Also, while not urgent, we typically require a minimum 9–12 month deprecation window for breaking public API changes for customers in regulated verticals. If Redwood can commit to something similar it will simplify our customer communications.

Cheers,
Liam
Director, Integrations
Orbis Ecosystems
Attachments: orbis-adapter-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbis-ecosys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood API changes — impact to Orbis adapter

Hi Liam — thanks for the matrix and the clear asks. Short answers up-front, followed by a proposal: 

- Deprecation notice: our baseline policy for public hosted endpoints is 12 months for breaking changes; we can extend to 18 months for strategic partners with active integrations (Orbis looks like a good candidate).
- Compatibility matrix: we'll produce an adapter-facing compatibility matrix that maps SDK/API surfaces to deprecation buckets (Stable / Maintenance / Breaking). Expect a first draft within 5 business days.
- Rollouts & fallbacks: the runtime supports staged rollouts by region and model variant; for Dedicated tenants we can coordinate canary windows and an optional automatic fallback to a pinned model if a request fails validation. We'll document the behavior.

Proposal / next steps:
1) Redwood will produce a partner-facing compatibility matrix + policy doc (deliverable: rdw-partner-sdk-deprecation-draft.pdf).
2) Joint sync on Wed 14 Jan 2026 at 09:30 PT (30 min) to walk matrix and ask/answer integration edge cases.
3) Redwood to propose a partner SLA addendum for Orbis if you commit to joint customer announcements.

If that works for you I'll loop in Vanessa (policy and partner ops) and our API product lead after the sync.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Strategic Partnerships 
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@orbis-ecosys.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood API changes — impact to Orbis adapter

Hi Liam / team — following Avery's note and our internal review, attaching a draft policy and an initial compatibility taxonomy. Key points from our side: 

- Versioning convention: we will adopt a hybrid semantic tag: MAJOR.MINOR+compat where MAJOR increments for breaking surface changes, MINOR for additive behavior, and +compat is an optional partner label (e.g., 2.3+orbis).
- Deprecation windows: default 12 months; strategic partners can request 6–18 month windows depending on mutual commitments. For Orbis we propose 15 months for the most disruptive surfaces you flagged (stream framing, multiplex APIs).
- Grace & canary: Redwood will perform a 2-week canary in a subset of regions and a 30-day staged rollback period where we will route failing requests to the previous compatible model variant for Dedicated tenants. We will provide telemetry hooks so Orbis can observe fail rates.
- Breaking change mitigation: we will publish adapter test vectors and a CI job template (GitHub Actions) that partners can run against pre-release builds.

Action items in the draft (rdw-partner-sdk-deprecation-draft.pdf):
- Redwood: deliver compatibility matrix with API-to-adapter mappings (5 business days)
- Orbis: mark high-priority adapter endpoints in the attached matrix and confirm minimum deprecation window per endpoint
- Joint: schedule public communication and SDK bump cadence after your sign-off

On the sync: Wed 14 Jan at 09:30 PT still works for us. If you prefer Thu we can also accommodate.

On a practical note, please confirm the HubSpot deal (ORB-2026-034) is correct so we can produce a partner SLA addendum that references the right account.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: rdw-partner-sdk-deprecation-draft.pdf (policy draft), adapter-taxonomy-example.csv

Avery / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. Orbis is comfortable with the proposed 15-month window for the stream framing change, and the hybrid semver label (+orbis) is workable for our release automation. A couple of small asks before we mark this as signed-off: 

- Can Redwood provide a short, customer-facing announcement template that Orbis can co-brand? We need that to prep our account teams.
- For the canary period, can we get read-access to the telemetry dashboard you mentioned (even if limited) so our SREs can watch the metrics live?

If you can attach the co-branded announcement draft and a read-only telemetry invite we can confirm by EOD Monday and proceed to update our adapter CI. We'll also update the attached adapter matrix with endpoint priorities and return it in the next 48 hours.

Thanks again — looking forward to the sync on Wed.
